assessment_review.scope_limit: Distinguish finite sampled rotation from a continuous rotating object; frequencies separated by fs are observationally equivalent. At zero frequency no cycle exists: the guarded finite samples-per-cycle readout is not a physical cycle count.
An interpolated display is a reconstruction assumption, not an independent observation of the analog waveform.
At Nyquist, the signed endpoint convention is ambiguous; finite real samples alone cannot resolve the original analog frequency.
The ideal 6.02 B+1.76 dB law assumes a full-scale sinusoid and a suitable quantization-error model; it is not a universal measured SQNR.
A finite seeded record is not an ensemble proof. Distinguish impulsive outliers, correlated noise and deterministic interference before choosing a noise model.
A finite displayed impulse response truncates the tail. Superposition and time invariance must hold before an impulse probe can characterize arbitrary inputs.
Record boundaries require explicit zero extension; circular wraparound would invent early echoes.
The lag sign follows the declared correlation convention. The largest peak in one noisy record does not establish detection probability.
A stable-looking short plot does not prove pole stability. A pole reaching the unit circle changes the long-time conclusion.
A finite filter has transition bands and edge transients. Do not claim perfect rejection or reconstruction from a single interior trace.
Changing record length changes the observation duration as well as the grid. The peak-bin estimate is quantized and is not the true frequency for every offset.
A lower plotted floor may hide gain normalization. Compare equivalent units and gain corrections before interpreting amplitude or noise power.
Peak interpolation can improve a single-tone estimate without resolving two tones. Display-bin spacing and physical resolution are separate quantities.
Welch smoothing reduces variance under stationarity assumptions. More overlap alone does not multiply independent information or remove bias from a nonstationary record.
A bright ridge's time coordinate depends on frame alignment. Edge padding and low-energy frames need separate interpretation.
The Hilbert construction does not make every multicomponent signal admit a unique physical instantaneous frequency.
A difference term outside the retained passband is attenuated. A real mixer does not preserve the same signed-frequency information as a complex one.
Complex sampling avoids conjugate overlap only within its chosen bandwidth and convention; it does not abolish aliasing.
A calibration inferred from unsuitable or changing data may not transfer. Image rejection is finite and must be stated with its signal/noise assumptions.
A single favorable realization cannot establish accuracy or a bound. Identify the repeated-trial population and any reliability gate.
Envelope recovery assumes a nonnegative envelope and suitable carrier separation. A spectral sideband diagram alone does not prove a demodulator recovered the message.
Sample-to-sample phase change must remain interpretable before differentiation. Aliased phase increments can give a smooth but wrong frequency estimate.
Symbol error and bit error are distinct. A seeded constellation is illustrative; probability claims require repeated independent decisions.
An infinite-duration zero-ISI property is only approximated by truncated filters. Sampling at the wrong delay can obscure an otherwise correct matched filter.
A known synthetic channel and stationary noise are assumptions. Recovery here does not demonstrate adaptation to an unknown time-varying channel.
A reference that contains desired-signal leakage can cancel the quantity we want. One bounded run does not certify every input covariance or step size.
Zero observed errors does not imply zero error probability. State the interval and independent trial count, especially in rare-event regimes.
A theoretical estimator limit depends on model and regularity assumptions. It is not a guaranteed error for every finite record or selected subset.
The ideal budget omits environment-dependent propagation and target variability. A numerical margin is not a measured detection range.
Two-way travel gives the factor of two. Fractional-delay interpolation, sampling and the retained waveform bandwidth each have separate error limits.
Resolution depends on the target pair, sidelobes and criterion, not only the nominal c/(2B) scale.
A processing-gain number is incomplete without input/output noise bandwidth and pulse-energy normalization.
Keep strong-target normalization and weak-target offset fixed during the comparison; otherwise visibility changes have multiple causes.
The ambiguity surface describes a waveform and convention, not a complete detector or multi-target scene.
A second hypothesis or diversity is required to resolve ambiguity. The recorded fast-time span need not equal the full PRI range interval.
Pulse sampling aliases Doppler outside its unambiguous interval. State the approach/recession convention before interpreting sign.
The matrix is a finite observation. Its displayed range span, range resolution and PRF ambiguity interval are different quantities.
Subtracting adjacent range cells is a different operation. Normalization is needed before comparing target power or output SNR across cancellers.
Combining detections from multiple dwells does not by itself solve every ambiguity or establish a joint false-alarm rate.
Coherence and independent noise are assumptions. A drifting target or oscillator can prevent the nominal gain.
The model is synthetic and finite. Matching its mean power does not validate a real clutter distribution or target fluctuation model.
Finite target separations and window shape determine resolution; finer bins alone do not guarantee two separable peaks.
A stationary distribution underlies a fixed-threshold calibration; nonstationary clutter can invalidate that calibration without a coding error.
ROC points need trial counts and uncertainty. Correlated searched cells change count variance and invalidate naive independent-binomial intervals.
The exact alpha law assumes independent homogeneous cells and a training set independent of the CUT.
A guard width adequate for one waveform or window can be insufficient after the target response broadens.
The calibration and fluctuating-target assumptions must match between detectors; a single scene's hit count is insufficient.
Neither rule universally dominates. Applying CA's multiplier to a different reference statistic breaks a fair equal-Pfa comparison.
The outlier-capacity argument concerns large contamination, not every texture or correlated-background failure.
Untestable is different from a tested miss. A map's displayed border should not be included blindly in a Pfa denominator.
Use truth only for offline labeling. Do not feed target truth into the operational detector to manufacture a favorable verdict.
Confidence coverage refers to repeated experiments under assumptions. One interval containing the target rate does not prove a detector is universally calibrated.
Cluster connectivity and target response can merge multiple physical targets. Report count is not a direct truth count.
Gain choices encode a tracking compromise. A deterministic trajectory does not establish robustness to every maneuver or clutter condition.
One mean NIS near its expected value is a diagnostic, not an ensemble consistency proof. Model mismatch can persist despite plausible position tracks.
EKF linearization is local. Large uncertainties, poor geometry or an incorrect Jacobian can invalidate the covariance interpretation.
A valid gate only declares plausibility. It does not prove identity or eliminate clutter ambiguity.
A deleted identifier and a newly initiated track must not be silently treated as uninterrupted identity.
Offline truth labels diagnose identity errors; they are unavailable to the operational association step.
The mode library bounds the maneuvers represented. Favorable results for this trajectory do not prove arbitrary maneuver coverage.
Wrapped phases can make distinct directions indistinguishable. State angle origin and sign before applying a steering vector.
A sharp maximum does not establish unique direction when spatial aliases are present.
Unresolved coherent or closely spaced sources can merge. A scan peak is conditioned on the assumed array geometry and calibration.
The linear calibration is local and bounded. Extrapolating its slope beyond the supported region invents accuracy.
A small constraint residual is necessary but does not prove high output SINR or correct steering.
A narrow pseudospectrum peak is not a calibrated confidence interval or an unconditional resolution guarantee.
One-angle calibration may leave direction-dependent coupling residuals. Recovery in the retained fixture does not establish all-angle calibration.
This small synthetic processor does not certify operational STAP convergence, calibration or clutter stationarity.
The stationary single-target formula neglects Doppler. Sign, overlap and beat aliasing must be checked before interpreting a range estimate.
A longer coherent dwell assumes sufficiently stable motion and phase. More plotted samples alone do not establish independent resolution gains.
One chirp's beat alone cannot identify both unknowns without additional assumptions or measurements.
The two-slope algebra does not solve multi-target association. Magnitudes alone may discard the sign information required by the equations.
The virtual-array interpretation assumes a coherent target model over the switching schedule. Acceleration and unresolved targets can invalidate simple correction.
The synthetic kinematic signature is not evidence that a classifier can identify real people, activities or targets.
Image focus relies on the assumed path and geometry. This point-scatterer model omits extended-scene scattering and real navigation errors.
Range compression alone does not focus cross-range. A narrower range trace does not establish two-dimensional image resolution.
Separate aperture extent, sampling density and image-grid spacing; adding grid pixels is not equivalent to adding coherent measurements.
Interpolation and finite support limit recovery. Data shifted outside the observed range window cannot be reconstructed by alignment alone.
Nominal resolution formulas assume the stated geometry and adequate sampling. Report the measured criterion and sidelobes alongside width.
Reference-based autofocus relies on scene and phase-screen assumptions. It is not a general solution for spatially varying motion errors.
A rigid rotating point-scatterer model and known rotation convention bound the interpretation. Unknown rotation scale creates cross-range ambiguity.
Excess path is not distance from a single sensor. Localization additionally requires transmitter/receiver geometry and enough independent constraints.
The small synthetic array and pulse ensemble support a mechanism demonstration, not deployment-level STAP performance or a universal training requirement.

This is a pulsed-radar chain. It does not execute FMCW, virtual-array, SAR, ISAR or passive branches, and requested homogeneous-cell Pfa is not a guarantee in the correlated clutter scene. A model-valid toggle flag is not a target-detection or tracking-success verdict; use the computed counts and errors.

scoped_review: Executed full state-feedback acceleration with position and velocity terms, dimensioned gains, analytic derivatives and DC/pole checks.
Executed declared-cost CARE LQR and actual coupled plant/observer states; analytic CARE/spectrum and state-transition checks.
Measured the actual integral-state peak consistently, bounded manual/automatic actuation and explicitly censored recovery; independent piecewise-affine replay.
Integrated double-well dynamics and damping work; independent implicit solver plus energy, phase-field and zero-damping checks.
Recomputed the barrier filter at every sampled state; independent linear/geometric trajectory and full-history safety checks.
Constructed real gain-table knots and measured interpolation errors; independent secant evaluator plus knot, off-grid and refinement checks.
Integrated nonlinear cancellation residual with an explicit departure event; independent reciprocal-state trajectory/event and exact-cancellation checks.
Evaluated dimensionless sensitivity over the declared uncertainty and frequency grid; independent complex transfer and stability/pole checks.
Solved actual bounded horizon optimization and applied receding-horizon moves; independent Bellman policy plus full-plan feasibility, objective and KKT checks.
Generated excitation, fitted an ARX model and evaluated separate held-out free-run data; independent convolution/normal equations and rank/recovery checks.
Executed recursive least-squares gain, estimate and covariance updates; independent weighted batch information and zero-excitation checks.
Constructed and transformed actual sigma points; independently checked Gaussian moments and distinct mean/covariance weights. Scope is the transform component, not recursive UKF.

known_issue: The claimed RTS smoother multiplies filtered covariance by a fixed 0.65 instead of executing a forward filter and backward smoother.
Quaternion norm and rotation orthogonality errors are fixed constants; no quaternion-to-matrix transformation is evaluated.
GNSS position and clock errors are algebraic dilution formulas; the claimed pseudorange position/clock solve is not executed.
GNSS/INS uncertainty is reduced by a fixed 0.35 factor rather than an error-state covariance update and state reset.
The post-exclusion residual is multiplied by a fixed 0.15 without excluding a measurement and recomputing the navigation solution.
The guidance comparison reports an explicitly named miss proxy, but the trajectories and variants are not integrated; its scope and cumulative interpretation need revision.
Terminal error is assigned from an acceleration shortfall; the terminal dynamics are not propagated and the displayed violation is not measured from applied commands.

scoped_review: Executed calibration identification, feedback and scalar estimation across three stressed plants; independent normal-equation/information-form replay and plant/rank checks.
Executed exact planar motion, GNSS/inertial updates, waypoint guidance and freshness holds; independent complex-arc replay and timing/turn checks.
Executed timestamped command delivery, drop burst, old-packet rejection, plant feedback and fail-zero watchdog; independent arrival reconstruction and zero-fault checks.

known_issue: Constraint residual and tangent dimension are assigned without constructing the constraint Jacobian or projecting a configuration velocity.
Orthogonality, determinant and composition errors are algebraic surrogates without constructing and composing rigid transforms.
Power-invariance and adjoint round-trip errors are assigned without transforming an actual twist/wrench pair.
Singular values and finite-difference errors are assigned from elbow-angle formulas without constructing the Jacobian or differencing kinematics.
Task error and null-space leakage are parameter formulas without executing a Jacobian pseudoinverse and null-space projection.
The virtual-power error is assigned from force times lever arm, which has torque units; no joint/Cartesian velocity power comparison is executed.
Inertia eigenvalue and skew-identity error are assigned without constructing inertia and Coriolis matrices.
Payload error, regressor conditioning and inverse-dynamics residual are formulas of the guess and excitation rather than an identified model and held-out torque calculation.
The cubic trajectory duration omits its 1.5 peak-velocity factor, while the nominal limit-violation metric is forced to zero and plotted acceleration omits time scaling.
Joint/task tracking and torque metrics use condition-number formulas rather than executing the stated kinematics and feedback loops.
Computed-torque tracking and gravity residuals are algebraic surrogates rather than an integrated robot model with model-based compensation.
Operational-space inertia and residuals are assigned without forming the joint inertia, Jacobian or operational-space dynamics.
Contact responses and settling metrics use exponential surrogates instead of the declared impedance/admittance differential equations.
Hybrid motion/force residuals and projector error are assigned without constructing the surface-frame projectors or executing feedback.
Passivity energy and recovery are formulas of delay and force limit; no delayed work/energy trace is executed.
Swing-up time and balance error are algebraic surrogates; no underactuated dynamics, energy controller or balancing transition is executed.
Pinhole projection executes, but the near-plane violation metric is a fixed mode flag rather than a test of projected point depth.
Calibration errors are formulas of view count and distortion; no synthetic calibration views are fitted or independently reprojected.
Feature repeatability, descriptor distance and count are formulas of threshold and rotation; no image features or descriptors are computed.
Inlier and false-acceptance metrics are formulas of outlier fraction and threshold; no correspondence consensus model is fitted.
Stereo depth and uncertainty formulas execute, but the round-trip residual is fixed rather than computed from reprojection.
Pose and reprojection errors are formulas of noise and landmark count; no landmark pose solve is executed.
Occupancy and entropy metrics are formulas of beam count and probability rather than ray updates on an occupancy grid.
ICP residual, transform error and iteration count are algebraic surrogates; no point correspondence or registration iteration is executed.
Appearance and geometry gates execute, but map deformation is a fixed-factor residual formula rather than a recomputed graph solution.

scoped_review: Executed range observations, occupancy, graph replanning, timed hold/resume and continuous segment separation; independent breadth-first replay and geometric checks.
Executed calibrated reach, static support and timed contact control with exact spring work; independent kinematic/work replay and zero-tank checks.
